# SPHEREx → All-Sky Equirectangular VR Starfield: Feasibility Report
*(as of 2026-07-24)*

## Bottom line up front
- **What exists TODAY at IRSA:** Level 2 *spectral images* (per-exposure multi-extension FITS), released weekly, currently the **QR2** ("Quick Release 2") processing. These are individual pointings, not a mosaic.
- **What does NOT yet exist (promised):** The official **102-band all-sky spectral data cubes / mosaics** (HEALPix, Galactic coords). Per the SPHEREx map-making paper these are scheduled for the **Year-1 data release ~November 2026** via an IRSA "public mosaic tool." So in July 2026 you would be building your own mosaic OR waiting ~4 months for the official one.
- **The pretty "all-sky maps" NASA already published** (May 2025 onward) are **visualizations only** — spatial resolution deliberately reduced by ~1000×, not science-grade downloadables.
- **Feasibility verdict:** Mosaicking raw L2 yourself is possible but heavy (~2.3 million exposures over the mission; hundreds of thousands already public). For a VR starfield the **sane path is to wait for / use the official HEALPix all-sky cubes and reproject them to equirectangular (CAR)** with `reproject`/`healpy`. That is a single-GPU, few-hours job rather than a mosaicking pipeline project.

---

## 1. SPHEREx public data products at IRSA (mid-2026)

**Release cadence & status**
- **QR1**: weekly releases began **July 2025**. Now legacy (QR1 on AWS only through Jan 2026).
- **QR2**: weekly releases began **October 2025**, improved calibration, supersedes QR1. This is the current live product.
- **Latency:** data appears publicly **~60 days after observation**.
- First full all-sky *coverage* epoch was acquired early 2026 (survey runs May→Dec 2025 for pass 1). Four all-sky passes total over the 25-month mission (2 sky surveys/year).

**Level 2 Spectral Images (available now)**
- Format: **Multi-Extension FITS (MEF)**. **6 MEFs per sky pointing** (one per detector), **~70 MB each**, 6 extensions.
- Each detector image: **2040 × 2040 pixels, native ~6.15 arcsec/pixel** (≈ your 6.2"; note the PSF is oversampled internally at 0.615"/sub-pixel — don't confuse the two; the science pixel is 6.15").
- Extensions include: calibrated flux, per-pixel flags/status, variance map, zodiacal-light model, exposure-averaged PSF, and **spectral WCS** (which wavelength each pixel sampled — because of the Linear Variable Filters, wavelength varies across the array).
- Six bands 0.75–5.0 µm (Band1 0.75–1.09; Band2 1.10–1.62; Band3 1.63–2.41; Band4 2.42–3.82; Band5 3.83–4.41; Band6 4.42–5.00), R≈35–130. The 102 "colors" come from co-adding many exposures that sampled each sky position at different LVF wavelengths.
- Calibration products also public (gain, dark, PSF ~6 MB [101×101×121], dichroic, solid-angle maps, etc.).

**All-sky maps / data cubes (promised, not yet public)**
- Year-1 & Year-2 releases will include **102 single-color full-sky mosaics** ("Data Cube" product) — spatially+spectrally interpolated all-sky maps at 102 wavelengths.
- Projection: **HEALPix in Galactic coordinates** for science; the coverage-monitoring maps use Mollweide at Nside=1024 (3.4' pixels). Science full-sky products use HEALPix representation, delivered via an IRSA "public mosaic tool."
- **Scheduled ~November 2026** (Year-1). As of July 2026: **not released yet.**

**Rough full-sky download size (build-your-own from L2)**
- Mission total ≈ **2.3 million exposures**; 14 billion spectra; ~1.4 trillion voxels *per* all-sky pass. At ~70 MB × 6 detectors per pointing, the full L2 corpus is on the order of **hundreds of TB**. Even one complete sky pass of L2 is tens of TB. This is the main argument against DIY mosaicking.

---

## 2. Tooling

- **IRSA APIs:** IVOA **Simple Image Access v2 (SIA2)** endpoint `https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/SIA?` with collections `spherex_qr2` (wide), `spherex_qr2_deep` (deep), `spherex_qr2_cal` (calibration). Query by position/band/time/ID.
- **Python:** **`pyvo`** and **`astroquery`** (SIA2 + TAP). IRSA publishes tutorial notebooks (the "Introduction to SPHEREx Spectral Images" tutorial).
- **Cutout Service:** spatial subsets of the L2 MEFs by center + size (same HDU structure).
- **Bulk/cloud:** browsable dirs at `https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/ibe/data/spherex/qr2` (wget/curl); **AWS Open Data** bucket `s3://nasa-irsa-spherex` (`us-east-1`, no-sign-request) — mirrors QR2 `level2/`. Good if you run your V100 pod in/near AWS us-east-1.
- **Web GUI:** SPHEREx Data Explorer.
- **Reprojection/mosaic:** `reproject` (`reproject_from_healpix`/`reproject_to_healpix`, target `CAR`), `healpy` (`cartview`, `projview`), `astropy.wcs`. No dedicated "spherex" all-sky-mosaic PyPI package found; the SPHEREx pipeline paper describes an internal bin/coadd mosaicker not yet released as user tooling. No mature community all-sky SPHEREx mosaic exists yet (too early).

---

## 3. How popular all-sky renderings / colorizations are made

**NASA/JPL SPHEREx visualizations (SVS 31376, PIA26600)**
- Elliptical (Mollweide-style) all-sky projection; **resolution reduced ~1000×** from native.
- Two colorization schemes documented: (a) science/ISM view — 4 µm hot hydrogen → **blue**, 3.4 µm PAH dust → **red**; (b) stars/galaxies view — **short/medium/long wavelength → blue/green/red**. No public code, but the convention (short→blue, long→red) is the standard.

**Precedent pipelines you can copy**
- **Lupton et al. asinh RGB** (the canonical false-color method): asinh stretch preserves faint structure while not saturating bright cores — the de-facto standard for SDSS, unWISE, HiPS. (`astropy.visualization.make_lupton_rgb`.) Paper: astro-ph/0312483.
- **unWISE / WISE all-sky:** 2.75"/pix coadds at 3.4 & 4.6 µm (W1/W2), Meisner/Lang coadd methodology; a well-documented 2-band → color precedent very close to your SPHEREx use case.
- **Gaia DR2 "Sky in Colour":** built with **HEALPix + healpy**; flux/density maps binned to HEALPix (up to Nside=8192 ≈ 0.18 arcmin²/pixel), then plane-projected; interactive via GAVS. Good reference for HEALPix→image color compositing.
- **HEALPix → equirectangular (CAR)** is a solved problem: `reproject_from_healpix(..., <CAR WCS>)`; healpy `projview`. This is exactly the last step you need for a VR equirect texture.

---

## 4. Effort estimate — single V100 pod, astropy skills

**Two realistic paths:**

**Path A — Wait for / use official HEALPix all-sky cubes (recommended).**
- Available ~Nov 2026. Download 102 HEALPix maps (Galactic), pick your band-to-RGB triplets, apply asinh/log stretch (Lupton), `reproject_from_healpix → CAR`, tile into equirect layers.
- Effort: **days**, not months. Trivially fits a single V100 (it's mostly I/O + reprojection, GPU barely needed except for compositing/upscaling). Multiple wavelength/depth layers = just choose different band groupings.

**Path B — Build your own mosaic from L2 now.**
- You'd query L2 via SIA2, handle each exposure's **per-pixel spectral WCS** (wavelength varies across array), regrid/bin onto a common HEALPix grid per wavelength channel, coadd with hit-count/variance tracking, mask zodiacal light. This replicates the mission's L2→L3 mapmaker.
- Effort: **weeks–months**; data volume tens–hundreds of TB; the wavelength-assignment/coaddition bookkeeping is the hard part, not the compute. Feasible on one V100 only if you restrict to a sky region or a few bands. Not recommended for a first all-sky VR texture.

**Coverage gaps / solar exclusion (important for early releases):**
- SPHEREx surveys in great circles roughly perpendicular to the Sun; there are **solar-exclusion / partial-coverage regions** and the ecliptic poles get very deep coverage (the two "deep fields"), while a full uniform all-sky pass only completes every ~6 months. Early QR data has **uneven depth and coverage holes** — a mid-2026 DIY mosaic would have visible gaps/seams. The official Year-1 cube is specifically the point at which full, gap-filled all-sky coverage is guaranteed. (IRSA docs don't tabulate the exclusion zones explicitly; the mission papers describe the survey geometry.)

    """CAR galactic WCS for a horizontal strip whose bottom FITS row is global
    row0 (0-based, bottom-up). CRVAL2 must stay 0 for CAR, so the latitude
    band is selected purely via CRPIX2."""
    full_h = full_h or height
    step = 360.0 / width
    return {
        "NAXIS1": width, "NAXIS2": height, "WCSAXES": 2,
        "CTYPE1": "GLON-CAR", "CTYPE2": "GLAT-CAR",
        "CUNIT1": "deg", "CUNIT2": "deg",
        "CRVAL1": 0.0, "CRVAL2": 0.0,
        "CDELT1": -step, "CDELT2": step,
        "CRPIX1": width / 2 + 0.5, "CRPIX2": full_h / 2 + 0.5 - row0,
    }


def expected_bytes(width, height):
    """FITS: 2880-byte header block(s) + big-endian float32 data, 2880-padded.
    Lower bound (>= 1 header block) is enough for resume/size checks."""
    data = width * height * 4
    return 2880 + ((data + 2879) // 2880) * 2880


def fetch_one(hips, wcs, dst):
    """Download one hips2fits FITS render, atomically, with mirror fallback."""
    if os.path.exists(dst) and os.path.getsize(dst) >= expected_bytes(wcs["NAXIS1"], wcs["NAXIS2"]):
        log(f"  skip {os.path.basename(dst)} (present)")
        return 0
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({"hips": hips, "format": "fits", "wcs": json.dumps(wcs)})
    mpx = wcs["NAXIS1"] * wcs["NAXIS2"] / 1e6
    part = dst + ".part"
    for attempt in range(6):
        svc = SERVICES[min(attempt // 3, 1)]  # 3 tries primary, then mirror
        try:
            t0 = time.time()
            req = urllib.request.Request(f"{svc}?{q}", headers={"User-Agent": UA})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900) as r, open(part, "wb") as f:
                while chunk := r.read(1 << 20):
                    f.write(chunk)
            os.replace(part, dst)
            mb = os.path.getsize(dst) / 1e6
            log(f"  {os.path.basename(dst)}: {mb:.0f} MB ({mpx:.1f} Mpx) in {time.time()-t0:.0f}s")
            return mb
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as e:
            wait = 15 * (attempt + 1)
            log(f"  !! {os.path.basename(dst)} attempt {attempt+1} ({svc.split('/')[2]}): {e} — retry in {wait}s")
            time.sleep(wait)
    raise RuntimeError(f"all attempts failed for {dst}")


def run(stage):
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    if stage == "test":
        wcs = strip_wcs(512, 128, row0=64, full_h=256)  # off-center strip: exercises CRPIX2 math
        fetch_one(BANDS["W1"], wcs, os.path.join(OUT, "W1_test.fits"))
        return
    if stage == "preview":
        for band, hips in BANDS.items():
            fetch_one(hips, strip_wcs(PREVIEW_W, PREVIEW_H),
                      os.path.join(OUT, f"{band}_preview.fits"))
        return
    # fetch: 4 strips x 2 bands, bottom-up
    sh = FULL_H // N_STRIPS
    total = 0
    for band, hips in BANDS.items():
        for s in range(N_STRIPS):
            wcs = strip_wcs(FULL_W, sh, row0=s * sh, full_h=FULL_H)
            total += fetch_one(hips, wcs, os.path.join(OUT, f"{band}_strip{s}.fits")) or 0
    log(f"DONE — fetched {total:.0f} MB this run -> {OUT}")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("stage", choices=["test", "preview", "fetch"])
    args = ap.parse_args()
    run(args.stage)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compose N all-sky band maps (FITS strips from fetch_unwise.py) into an RGB equirect.

Source-agnostic "band maps -> RGB" stage: the unWISE W1/W2 recipe is one named
config; the SPHEREx Year-1 102-band cubes drop in later as another (different
matrix/scales, same code path). Colorization is the Lang/Legacy-Surveys
convention (legacypipe _unwise_to_rgb): color-preserving asinh — luminance is
stretched, per-band ratios are kept, which is what tames the galactic bulge
without greying its color.

  python3 upscale/allsky_rgb.py --preview                 # 4096 preview -> deepsky_prev/
  python3 upscale/allsky_rgb.py --preview --simulate-tonemap   # post-Reinhard look
  python3 upscale/allsky_rgb.py                           # full res -> _raw/unwise/*.tif

FITS is hand-parsed (single primary HDU, BITPIX -32/-64) — the pipeline env has
only numpy+PIL, and astropy for two keywords is not worth the dependency
(precedent: backdrop_tool.py hand-parses Radiance RGBE).
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
REPO = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "scripts"))
from backdrop_tool import tonemap                                    # noqa: E402

Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
FITS_DIR = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/_raw/unwise/fits")
OUT_TIF = os.path.join(REPO, "Float/Resources/Textures/_raw/unwise/unwise_w1w2_equirectangular.tif")
PREV_DIR = os.path.join(HERE, "deepsky_prev")

# band order matches the row order of `matrix` columns; matrix rows are R, G, B.
UNWISE = dict(
    bands=["W1", "W2"],
    scales=[50.0, 50.0],
    matrix=[[0.0, 1.0],   # R = W2 (4.6um — dust)
            [0.5, 0.5],   # G = synthetic mean
            [1.0, 0.0]],  # B = W1 (3.4um — stars)
    mn=-1.0, mx=100.0, arcsinh=1.0,
)


def log(msg):
    print(f"[{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] {msg}", flush=True)


def read_fits(path):
    """Primary HDU of a hips2fits render -> float32 array (FITS row 0 = bottom)."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        raw = f.read()
    hdr = {}
    end = 0
    for blk in range(0, len(raw), 2880):
        for i in range(blk, blk + 2880, 80):
            card = raw[i:i + 80].decode("ascii", "replace")
            key = card[:8].strip()
            if key == "END":
                end = blk + 2880
                break
            if "=" in card:
                hdr[key] = card.split("=", 1)[1].split("/")[0].strip()
        if end:
            break
    w, h, bitpix = int(hdr["NAXIS1"]), int(hdr["NAXIS2"]), int(hdr["BITPIX"])
    dt = {-32: ">f4", -64: ">f8"}[bitpix]
    n = w * h * abs(bitpix) // 8
    return np.frombuffer(raw[end:end + n], dtype=dt).reshape(h, w).astype(np.float32)


def load_band(band, preview):
    """Assemble one band: single preview file, or bottom-up full-res strips."""
    if preview:
        return read_fits(os.path.join(FITS_DIR, f"{band}_preview.fits"))
    strips = sorted(p for p in os.listdir(FITS_DIR)
                    if p.startswith(f"{band}_strip") and p.endswith(".fits"))
    if not strips:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no {band}_strip*.fits in {FITS_DIR} — run fetch_unwise.py fetch")
    return np.vstack([read_fits(os.path.join(FITS_DIR, s)) for s in strips])


def compose(bands, matrix, scales, mn, mx, arcsinh, bg_pct=None):
    """Lang color-preserving asinh: stretch the band mean, keep per-band ratios,
    then mix channels via `matrix` and normalize to the (mn, mx) cuts."""
    imgs = []
    for a, s in zip(bands, scales):
        a = np.nan_to_num(a, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
        if bg_pct is not None:
            a = np.clip(a - np.percentile(a, bg_pct), 0.0, None)
        imgs.append(a / s)
    mean = np.mean(imgs, axis=0)
    nlmap = lambda x: np.arcsinh(x * arcsinh) / np.sqrt(arcsinh)   # noqa: E731
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        gain = np.where(mean != 0, nlmap(mean) / mean, 0.0)
    lo, hi = nlmap(mn), nlmap(mx)
    stretched = [(im * gain - lo) / (hi - lo) for im in imgs]
    rgb = np.clip(np.tensordot(np.asarray(matrix), np.asarray(stretched), axes=1), 0.0, 1.0)
    return (np.moveaxis(rgb, 0, -1) * 255.0 + 0.5).astype(np.uint8)


def seam_check(rgb):
    d = float(np.abs(rgb[:, 0].astype(np.int16) - rgb[:, -1].astype(np.int16)).mean())
    log(f"  wrap seam |col0 - col-1| mean: {d:.2f} (8-bit levels)")
    if d > 8.0:
        log("  !! seam differs noticeably — check strip WCS before shipping")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--preview", action="store_true", help="use *_preview.fits, JPG only")
    ap.add_argument("--bg-pct", type=float, default=None,
                    help="per-band percentile background subtraction (e.g. 30)")
    ap.add_argument("--auto-cut", action="store_true",
                    help="derive mn/mx from data percentiles (if flux units are off)")
    ap.add_argument("--simulate-tonemap", action="store_true",
                    help="preview through the pipeline's Reinhard tonemap")
    ap.add_argument("--exposure", type=float, default=0.0, help="stops, with --simulate-tonemap")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = dict(UNWISE)
    band_names = cfg.pop("bands")
    bands = []
    for b in band_names:
        a = load_band(b, args.preview)
        log(f"  {b}: {a.shape[1]}x{a.shape[0]}, median {np.nanmedian(a):.1f}")
        bands.append(a)
    if args.auto_cut:
        ref = np.nan_to_num(np.mean(bands, axis=0))
        cfg["mn"], cfg["mx"] = np.percentile(ref, 1) / cfg["scales"][0], np.percentile(ref, 99.9) / cfg["scales"][0]
        log(f"  auto cuts: mn={cfg['mn']:.2f} mx={cfg['mx']:.2f}")

    rgb = compose(bands, bg_pct=args.bg_pct, **cfg)
    rgb = rgb[::-1]                      # FITS bottom-up -> image top-down
    seam_check(rgb)

    if args.simulate_tonemap:
        srgb = rgb.astype(np.float32) / 255.0
        lin = np.where(srgb <= 0.04045, srgb / 12.92, ((srgb + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4)
        rgb = tonemap(lin, exposure=args.exposure)

    os.makedirs(PREV_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    im = Image.fromarray(rgb, "RGB")
    prev = im if im.width <= 2048 else im.resize((2048, 1024), Image.LANCZOS)
    tag = "_tonemap" if args.simulate_tonemap else ""
    jpg = os.path.join(PREV_DIR, f"unwise_w1w2{tag}.jpg")
    prev.save(jpg, quality=90)
    log(f"  preview -> {jpg}")

    if not args.preview:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(OUT_TIF), exist_ok=True)
        im.save(OUT_TIF, compression="tiff_adobe_deflate")
        log(f"  full res -> {OUT_TIF} ({os.path.getsize(OUT_TIF)/1e6:.0f} MB)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Fixed and rebuilt. The banding was 8-bit quantization contouring: the diffuse glow around the galactic plane is a very smooth latitude gradient, and at the darkened cuts one 8-bit step spanned about 2° of sky — wide horizontal plateaus that HEIC compression then sharpened into visible bands (real photos mask this with sensor noise; our composed map was too clean).

Verified at each stage: the TIFF's background now varies every ~2 rows instead of holding ~100-row plateaus, the dither survives the HEIC q0.9 pack, and an 8×-boosted dark-sky crop from the shipped HEIC shows no contours — just uniform star grain and smooth glow falloff. The HEIC was repacked (68.2 MB) and the sim build succeeded, which also confirms your catalog/manifest pruning compiles clean.

Since the dither lives in the shared compose stage, the SPHEREx 102-band build in November inherits it automatically.

One thing I noticed in the boosted crop, for your headset pass: the brightest stars carry faint ring/halo ghosts — those are unWISE source artifacts around saturated stars, essentially invisible at normal levels, but worth a glance on device before you call the scene done.
